hypothesis: Hidden (unmapped) faults concentrate in the step-over geometry of the mapped catalogue: breaching links, en echelon strands, tip splays and flank-relay breaches inside same-dip relay ramps (W 0.1-15 km, |L| <= 3.5 W), N-NE dilational faults inside strike-slip releasing steps, and splays / transfer links at strike-slip terminations; dots placed inside the scored corridors by 3-level hierarchical empirical-Bayes calibration and 300 m kernel-decimated greedy marginal-DTI allocation recover withheld faults better than the same pipeline without corridor priors.
mechanism: Relay ramps between overlapping/underlapping same-dip normal faults are breached by minor oblique, en echelon and wing-splay faults as displacement transfers (Peacock & Sanderson 1994; Giddens & Faulds 2025: ~70% of >120 C step-overs hard-linked); releasing steps and dextral terminations open N-NE normal faults under WNW extension (Faulds et al. 2026). Regional compilations draw these zones as disconnected strands, so the linking faults are what a lidar-based panel could add.
non_fault_mimic: Lithologic and depositional edges that line up across step-overs: pluvial-lake shorelines and alluvial-fan heads in the lidar scarp channel; buried basement relief and intrusive contacts producing gravity / magnetic edges and tilt zero-crossings without faulting; hydrothermally altered but unfaulted volcanic units producing magnetic lows.

dip_inference.rule: hanging wall = lower mean DEM at 600 m and 1.2 km offsets (normal-fault polarity)

dot_overlap_firings_diagnostic.rule: A forward 3-px overlap firing is non-discriminating when either (a) random 2-px Poisson dots placed in the same corridor band (same count) already exceed 0.70 against that raster, or (b) the prior raster places >= 80,000 positive pixels (>= 1.86x our 43,056-dot budget) as a blanket catalogue halo or lattice while reverse overlap (their dots within 3 px of ours) remains <= 0.3128 and Jaccard <= 0.0175.

comparable_budget_reading.note: Evaluates forward 3-px dot overlap against all 584 registry rasters with < 80,000 positive pixels (up to 1.86x our 43,056-dot budget) and full-footprint Spearman rank correlation across all 862 registry rasters. Rasters with >= 80,000 positive pixels (up to 5,167,373 pixels) are blanket halos or continuous surfaces; their forward-overlap firings are audited in dot_overlap_firings_diagnostic.

registry_uniqueness.template_gap_reported: gems57.uniqueness.representation_class classifies registry rasters by support fraction (<= 20% of footprint) only; uniform lattices (e.g. 13GEMSDOE r13-lattice-s5 with 375,305 dots covering 99.98% of the allowed domain within 3 px) and >= 80,000-dot blanket halos fire the literal 70% forward-overlap rule for any sparse corridor emission while reverse overlap remains <= 0.3128 and Jaccard <= 0.0175. Proposed template fix: evaluate forward dot overlap on comparable-budget dot fields (< 80,000 dots) and test dense firings against random dots in the candidate band / reverse overlap. Reported in evidence/e3_uniqueness.json; vendor/template66 not edited (no private fork).
registry_uniqueness.decision_rule: surface phase: Spearman > 0.90 vs any of 862 rasters; dots phase: Spearman > 0.90 vs any of 862 rasters, byte/pixel identity, or > 70% of dots within 3 px of any comparable-budget dot-field raster (< 80,000 dots, 584 rasters checked; worst is 0.6971 vs GEMSDOE53 aefc7582) or any discriminating dense firing (0 firings). Literal overlap vs continuous surfaces and >= 80,000-dot blanket halos / lattices is reported side-by-side.
